lines: Morgan Kim
+1 (555) 010-8173 | morgan.kim@example.com | example.com/code/mkim
EDUCATION
Clearwater Institute of Technology | B.S. in Electrical Engineering | Metro City, USA | Sep 2017 - May 2021
EXPERIENCE
Voltline Robotics | Embedded Software Engineer | Metro City, USA | Mar 2023 - Jun 2025
- Improved update speed by 60% by compressing firmware images and resuming interrupted downloads.
- Wrote a hardware-in-the-loop test rig that ran 400 motor-control tests on every firmware build.
- Added a crash logger that saved the last 2 seconds of sensor data to flash, which found the root cause of 5 field failures.
- Sampled the motor's 5 kHz vibration signal at 8 kHz so the fault detector could capture it without aliasing.
- Fixed a race condition on the counter shared by the interrupt handler and the main loop by declaring the counter volatile.
- Rewrote the motor-controller firmware for a warehouse robot fleet of 300 units, cutting control-loop jitter from 120 to 15 microseconds and field motor faults by 60%.
Clearwater Sensors | Hardware Test Engineer | Metro City, USA | Apr 2022 - Feb 2023
- Automated end-of-line tests for a humidity sensor, cutting test time per unit from 90 to 25 seconds across 20,000 units a month.
- Traced a batch of early field failures to a solder-paste change; the findings updated the reflow profile and cut returns from 2.1% to 0.4%.
- Wrote the calibration procedure for the sensor line, cutting calibration drift complaints from 15 to 2 a quarter.
- Designed a test fixture that checked 8 boards at once, raising station throughput from 40 to 150 boards an hour.
PROJECTS
Low-Power Weather Station | Independent Project | C, STM32 | Jan 2025 - Present
- Engineered a next-generation, innovation-driven IoT solution that redefines sustainable environmental sensing.
- Cut average current from 4.2 mA to 0.9 mA by sleeping between readings and batching radio transmissions.
- Published the schematics and firmware openly, and a local school built two stations from them.
Formula Student Electric Car | Electronics Lead, Team of 12 | C | Sep 2019 - May 2021
- Worked on firmware and testing for the robot fleet's motor controllers.
- The CAN-bus firmware for the dashboard was written and tested against the motor controller before each race.
- Rewrote motor-control firmware for a fleet of about 300 robots, cutting control-loop jitter eightfold and motor faults by more than half.
SKILLS
Tools: C, C++, STM32, oscilloscopes, FPGA
Methods: firmware, hardware-in-the-loop testing, CAN, low-power design

items.says: Make sure the code link goes directly to work a reviewer can inspect.
Specify whether download, installation, or total update time became 60% faster.
items.because: Compression and resume address different parts of an update.

items.says: Give the conditions under which the speed improvement was measured.
items.because: The result is otherwise hard to interpret.

items.says: Clarify whether the 400 tests ran on every build.
items.because: That makes the scale of the rig easier to judge.

items.says: Clarify what the 400 tests covered.
items.because: That makes the value of the rig easier to judge.

items.says: Make the connection between the saved data and the five diagnosed failures precise.
items.because: “Found the root cause” may overstate what the logger alone established.

items.says: Sampling a 5 kHz signal at 8 kHz does not avoid aliasing.
items.because: An 8 kHz sample rate cannot directly capture a 5 kHz signal without aliasing.

items.says: Declaring the counter `volatile` does not by itself fix a race condition.
items.because: It does not provide atomic access or synchronization.

items.says: Check that the fault reduction is attributable to the fleet-firmware work.
Check that the 300-unit figure describes the fleet affected.
Verify that the 90-to-25-second figures cover the same portion of the test process.
Check whether the return-rate change can fairly be attributed to the reflow-profile update.
items.because: Other simultaneous changes may have affected returns.

items.says: Clarify whether complaints fell because of the calibration procedure.
Clarify whether the quarterly complaint counts cover comparable periods.
Make clear whether the throughput figures reflect comparable operating conditions.
items.because: Readers may otherwise expect an eightfold increase from the eight-board fixture.

items.says: The opening weather-station bullet uses promotional language without technical detail or evidence.
items.because: The two bullets below it provide more substance.

items.says: Add the current-measurement conditions if space permits.
items.because: Average current depends heavily on reading frequency, transmission schedule, and measurement duration.

items.says: Substantiate the school's adoption of the published work.
Ensure the linked repository makes the schematics and firmware easy to find.
The warehouse robot fleet does not appear to belong to a Formula Student electric-car project.
Clarify your personal contribution to the CAN-bus firmware.
Clarify your testing responsibility for the CAN-bus firmware.
The final Formula Student bullet repeats the Voltline fleet result.
items.because: It places that result under a project dated years earlier, creating a serious credibility problem.

items.says: Make sure your experience supports the listed C++, STM32, and FPGA skills.
items.because: The résumé currently gives little evidence for some of them.

items.says: Prioritize methods relevant to the roles you want.
items.because: “Firmware” is broad beside the more specific items.

items.says: Be ready to account for the period since your most recent job ended in June 2025.
items.because: That period may be a gap if this is your current résumé.
